chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from Ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The dowry (sadaq) is whatever they mutually agree upon, whether little or much."

key_terms.الصَّدَاقُ: The dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What determines the validity and amount of the dowry in Shia Islamic marriage law?
ai.summary: Reported by the prominent jurist Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith underscores the flexibility of the dowry (mahr) as a contractual element governed by mutual agreement (taradi) rather than rigid statutory limits. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the validity of the mahr depends on the consent of both parties, allowing for any amount to be agreed upon, thereby emphasizing the consensual nature of the marriage contract over fixed monetary values.
